title: Scale-dependent recoverability and prior-dominance frontier
purpose: Quantify which spatial and temporal modes of an Earth-interior state are recoverable from a declared observation layout, noise model and prior, and identify where the reported structure is dominated by regularization or unresolved cross-talk.

paradigm_shift.from: Choose one model resolution or spherical-harmonic truncation, invert, and display the resulting field.
paradigm_shift.to: Evaluate resolution as an empirical, scale-dependent property of the full inference setup. Publish a resolution frontier that trades spatial/temporal detail against recovery error, uncertainty calibration, prior sensitivity, observation coverage and compute cost.
paradigm_shift.principle: A rendered field's grid spacing, spectral truncation and numerical precision are not evidence of physical resolving power.
paradigm_shift.scientific_motivation: Published core-flow studies report that sensitivity to the prior and to the maximum spherical-harmonic degree varies by inferred feature; large-scale/transient features can be more robust while some slowly varying or higher-degree components remain substantially prior-dependent. Therefore, the recoverable subspace must be measured for each target and experiment rather than assumed universally.

research_basis.title: Effects of geodynamo priors and geomagnetic data on inverted core surface flows
research_basis.relevance: Compares geodynamo prior, field-model choice and secular-variation truncation; reports prior/setup sensitivity and feature-dependent robustness.

research_basis.title: Flow throughout the Earth's core inverted from geomagnetic observations and numerical dynamo models
research_basis.relevance: Reports resolution-matrix analysis and differences between twin-experiment recovery and real-data inversion, including modes whose estimates depend strongly on priors.

research_basis.title: A simple method for determining the spatial resolution of a general inverse problem
research_basis.relevance: Explains resolution matrices, their relation to averaging weights and resolution length, and limitations for large inverse problems.

research_basis.title: Metrics for evaluating the quality in linear atmospheric inverse problems: a case study of a trace gas inversion
research_basis.relevance: Connects averaging kernels and degrees of freedom for signal to information-content and resolution diagnostics.

research_basis.title: Spatial and temporal resolution of millennial scale geomagnetic field models
research_basis.relevance: Shows that temporal and spatial resolving power depends on data coverage and quality for long-time-span magnetic-field models.

linear_gaussian_reference.posterior_mean: m_post = Sp (H^T inverse(Se) y + inverse(Sa) m0)
requirements: Retain the full observation covariance, including correlated measurement errors.
Use dimensionless/scaled parameter coordinates and declare each scale.
Report diagonal resolution and off-diagonal cross-talk separately.
Report posterior uncertainty separately from data resolution; a tight prior may produce a tight posterior even when A shows that observations resolve little.
Do not infer global nonlinear identifiability from a local linear resolution matrix.

spectral_and_temporal_coordinates.spatial_modes: Use named spherical-harmonic degree/order or another declared basis, with poloidal/toroidal or equivalent physical mode identity kept explicit where relevant.
spectral_and_temporal_coordinates.temporal_modes: Use named periods/basis functions and explicit time support; distinguish acquisition cadence from recoverable temporal bandwidth.
spectral_and_temporal_coordinates.other_parameters: Include nuisance calibration offsets, source-separation terms or unresolved-scale terms when physically justified; label their status and avoid hiding them inside a residual bucket.

interpretation: The low-degree coordinate has a data-response resolution of 0.8 under this exact model.
The high-degree coordinate has data-response resolution of approximately 0.00990 and remains dominated by the stated prior despite a finite posterior variance.
A small posterior variance is not enough to claim the second coordinate is data-resolved; its variance is about 0.9901 under a unit prior variance while its data resolution is near zero.

acceptance_checks: Posterior covariance and resolution matrix match the analytic expressions within a preregistered numerical tolerance.
DOFS matches trace(A) and is not reported as the count of independently validated Earth-state parameters.
Parameter-order permutations permute matrix rows/columns consistently without changing semantic results.
A tight-prior ablation can produce a numerically tighter posterior while decreasing data attribution; the report must expose this rather than label it improved data resolution.
Off-diagonal examples are added in the next fixture tranche to prove that diagonal resolution alone can conceal cross-talk.

benchmark_stages.setup: Small analytical linear-Gaussian systems with known observation operators, correlated noise, tunable priors, and deliberately invisible/weakly visible modes.
must_show: Correct posterior covariance, averaging/resolution matrix, DOFS, and rank against direct analytic references.
Exact detection of planted null modes and correct behaviour under parameter reordering.
Correct distinction between posterior precision, data-resolution and prior dependence.

benchmark_stages.setup: Inject individual modes, pairs of modes, band-limited fields, transient time functions and spatially localized perturbations into frozen synthetic truth; forward-project through declared geometry, cadence, covariance, missingness and noise.
must_show: Amplitude attenuation, phase/time displacement, spatial spreading and mode cross-talk are reported by scale.
Recovery is evaluated on held-out truth states rather than only by in-sample residual.
Modes whose recovery is prior-dominated are labelled as such, not omitted from the diagnostics.
Results include repeated seeds and uncertainty intervals.

benchmark_stages.setup: Repeat the exact same synthetic observations across preregistered defensible prior strengths, spectra, parameterizations, spectral truncations and temporal regularizers.
must_show: Feature-by-feature data-resolution and prior sensitivity are separated.
Changes to high-degree truncation cannot silently create a higher qualified physical resolution.
Alternative parameterizations preserve units and named quantity-of-interest semantics.
Modes trading off against one another are exposed through off-diagonal resolution and posterior correlation.

benchmark_stages.setup: Use the active-observation policies in benchmark-adaptive-observation-design.json to choose candidate observation layouts under equal cost; compare resulting recoverability frontiers.
must_show: Report which modes gain resolution per unit cost, not only total EIG or trace(A).
A design does not win by improving already-resolved modes while sacrificing predeclared priority modes without making that trade-off visible.
Correlated duplicate observations are not counted as independent resolution gain.
The Pareto frontier covers resolution, held-out recovery error, uncertainty calibration, robustness and compute/acquisition cost.

benchmark_stages.setup: Only after GEO-DATA-001 independently verifies a documented public simulation payload, construct a reproducible adapter and then define a separate real-observation resolution evaluation with source-model leakage audit.
must_show: Exact source files, version, licence, digests, units, time support, parser and transform are pinned.
Simulation state is never labelled as real Earth truth.
Any reference field model is checked for overlapping observations before being used as an independent baseline.
Resolution estimates are reported with the model/prior/observation setup that produced them, not generalized as universal instrument capability.

measures: diagonal data-resolution by named mode
off-diagonal mode cross-talk and averaging-kernel concentration
DOFS / trace(A)
smallest resolved singular values and null-space directions
sensitivity of all above quantities to scale and numerical tolerance
mode-wise amplitude bias and recovery error
phase/timing error for transient or periodic features
spatial localization/spread and leakage into neighboring modes
frequency- and degree-dependent detection power
false discovery of absent injected modes
posterior mean displacement across prior variants
posterior covariance versus data-resolution separation
fraction of feature variance attributable to prior under a defined decomposition
rank and recoverability changes when data or prior information is ablated
resolution/recovery on held-out continuous time windows
resolution/recovery on held-out simulator configurations
coverage across sensor-layout/noise strata
degradation under declared forward-model discrepancy
Pareto frontier of detail versus recovery error, calibration, prior sensitivity and total cost
newly data-resolved priority modes per cost unit
forward-model evaluation count, wall time and peak memory
sensitivity of selected resolution to candidate design and model resolution

aspirational_targets_not_yet_acceptance_.target: 100% correct outcomes on the analytic linear-Gaussian and exact null-mode fixtures.
aspirational_targets_not_yet_acceptance_.qualification: Any failure here blocks more expensive benchmark stages.

aspirational_targets_not_yet_acceptance_.target: On predeclared detectable injected modes, at least 90% detection power with no more than 5% false detections across matched null controls.
aspirational_targets_not_yet_acceptance_.qualification: Freeze minimum amplitude, spatial/temporal scale, sample count and noise regime in advance; report a separate power curve instead of one aggregate value.

aspirational_targets_not_yet_acceptance_.target: Nominal 90%/95% credible intervals achieve predeclared coverage tolerance on held-out known-truth injections, without using posterior sharpness alone as a score.
aspirational_targets_not_yet_acceptance_.qualification: Report intervals and coverage separately by mode family, spatial scale, temporal period and sensor layout.

aspirational_targets_not_yet_acceptance_.target: Resolution diagnostics predict the ordering of empirical injection-recovery difficulty across registered modes with rank correlation >= 0.8.
aspirational_targets_not_yet_acceptance_.qualification: This is a proposed research target, not a known universal threshold; establish sample size and confidence intervals before the blind run.

aspirational_targets_not_yet_acceptance_.target: Report a Pareto frontier rather than one scalar winner when no policy dominates across detail, recovery error, calibration, prior sensitivity and cost.
aspirational_targets_not_yet_acceptance_.qualification: Any overall selection must declare the objective and weight/policy choices explicitly.

negative_controls: inject a null mode that has exactly zero sensitivity to all candidate observations
inject two distinct truth states with identical observations under the declared operator
tighten the prior until the posterior looks visually smooth and test that data-resolution does not falsely increase
vary the prior power spectrum while keeping observations fixed
truncate high-degree modes and check that displayed interpolation does not imply new information
duplicate measurements with correlated errors and ensure resolution is not overstated
shuffle time labels or add a clock offset to expose false temporal resolution
inject an omitted fine-scale component to test leakage into low-degree modes
alter a reference model to share test observations and ensure the baseline is not called independent

fields: exact generator/solver/model versions and manifest digest
observation operator, covariance, sampling layout and missingness identity
resolution matrix/averaging kernels/DOFS and their numerical tolerances
injection identities, amplitudes, phases, target scales and hidden truth reference
blind splits and PRNG seed policy
per-mode metrics, uncertainty intervals, negative-control outcomes and exclusions
frontier points and total compute/acquisition costs
exact code commit and qualification status

stop_rules: No claim of increased physical resolution solely because model truncation or rendered grid resolution increases.
No resolved/unresolved decision from diagonal averaging-kernel values alone if cross-talk materially affects the quantity of interest.
No comparison across parameter scalings unless dimensionless/scaling conventions are matched or transformed explicitly.
No posterior confidence or low residual may override a known non-identifiability or failed negative control.
No source-model baseline is labelled independent without an explicit held-out-data overlap audit.
No H4 qualification until dataset capture, hashing, licence, parsing and transform identity are independently established.

cross_project_ownership.sol_atlas: Own the resolution-frontier schema, scale-dependent claim semantics and later renderer overlays for data-resolved, prior-dominated and unresolved modes.
cross_project_ownership.symtropy: Generate known-truth mode injections, observation operators and coverage/noise/prior ablations.
cross_project_ownership.symthaea: Estimate posteriors, perform calibration and evaluate per-mode recovery; any HDC/LTC model must beat simple inversion/statistical baselines on held-out cases.
cross_project_ownership.mycelix: Reuse SCI-EVID-001 provenance/evidence lineage for manifests, results and derived claims; no second evidence ledger.

cross_project_implementation_note.note: Symtropy PR #1804 provides independent low-order analytic observation fixtures and a covariance-whitened observability oracle. Its dimensionless weak-mode fixture is a distinct reference from this document's H0 matrix diag(2.0, 0.1) with identity prior/noise; do not substitute one expected value set for the other.
